resources.string: Watches only the YouTube screen (and Facebook if enabled), taps the \"Skip ad\" button, can mute media volume while an ad plays, and can draw a tap-through blackout shield over unskippable or sponsored posts. Each feature can be switched off in the app. Uses no network access.
Finish the quick 3-step setup below to dismiss ads automatically.
Finish the quick 3-step setup below to dismiss ads automatically.
Protection paused via accessibility shortcut. Tap shortcut to resume.
Monitoring YouTube. Ads and audio disruptions are dismissed seamlessly.
1. Open accessibility settings, tap Hush Service, and press OK on the prompt.
2. Open App info -> tap 3 dots (⋮) -> Allow restricted settings (confirm with PIN/fingerprint).
3. Return here and turn Hush Service ON.
ADB fallback: adb shell appops set com.njk.adskipper ACCESS_RESTRICTED_SETTINGS allow
Taps the Skip button instantly when available.
Silences media audio during promotional segments.
Covers unskippable ad frames with a touch-through blackout shield.
Local on-device DNS filter. Never sends your traffic anywhere.
VPN permission revoked by another app — tap to re-enable
Hush filters known ad trackers directly on your device via a local loopback VPN. Nothing is logged, tracked, or sent to any remote server.
Overlays a tap-through blackout shield over sponsored feed stories in the Facebook app.

This feature monitors the Facebook app screen to detect sponsored items and overlay a blackout shield. Because Facebook regularly updates its layouts, some ads or Reels might not be caught, and minor scroll flicker may occur. No network, VPN, or data collection is used.
Hush needs notification permission to keep the local DNS ad filter running smoothly in the background while the screen is off.
Reads only targeted app screens. No remote network logs.
